newsitem.title: USA: Entergy withdraws from transition talks.
newsitem.headline: Entergy withdraws from transition talks.

text.p: Entergy Corp said Thursday negotiations with ALERT have been unproductive and the company is withdrawing from further talks with the group of large electricity users on its Transition to Competition filing.

"Judged by the negotiated and legislated outcomes in other states, it is clear to us that ALERT is not ready to discuss a reasonable settlement of the critical economic and operational issues in any meaningful sense," said Entergy Louisiana Inc President John Cordaro.

"In fact, during the negotiation period, your organization has engaged in vicious and inflammatory attacks on our company," he added in a letter to ALERT announcing the utility's withdrawal from the talks. Entergy released his comments in a statement.
"In sum, we question ALERT's sincerity in these negotiations and whether it is negotiating in good faith," he said.
Entergy and ALERT, at the request of Governor Foster, in April began discussions about issues related to Entergy's Transition to Competition filing.
During the discussions, Cordaro said, ALERT was "more interested in actively working against the best interests of a potential settlement."
Cordaro told ALERT, "It is evident from the actions of ALERT and the positions taken by your group that further negotiations at the time would be fruitless."
